import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/sleep_health.csv')

# Set a clean and professional seaborn style
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="viridis")

# Define a logical order for BMI categories for better visualization flow
bmi_order = ['Normal Weight', 'Normal', 'Overweight', 'Obese']

# Ensure 'BMI Category' is a categorical type with the specified order
# This helps in consistent plotting order across facets
df['BMI Category'] = pd.Categorical(df['BMI Category'], categories=bmi_order, ordered=True)

# Create a relational plot (scatter plot) to visualize the relationship between
# Sleep Duration, Quality of Sleep, and Stress Level, faceted by BMI Category.
# This allows for a multi-dimensional view of how these factors interact.
g = sns.relplot(
    data=df,
    x="Sleep Duration",
    y="Quality of Sleep",
    hue="Stress Level",  # Color points by Stress Level (continuous scale)
    col="BMI Category",  # Create separate columns for each BMI Category
    kind="scatter",
    palette="viridis",   # Use a perceptually uniform color palette
    col_wrap=2,          # Wrap columns after 2 plots to make the layout more compact
    height=4,            # Height of each individual facet
    aspect=1.2,          # Aspect ratio of each individual facet
    col_order=bmi_order, # Ensure facets appear in the defined BMI order
    s=70,                # Set marker size for better visibility
    alpha=0.8,           # Add some transparency to reveal point density
    facet_kws={'sharex': False, 'sharey': False} # Allow independent axes for better comparison within each category
)

# Set a comprehensive title for the entire figure
g.fig.suptitle(
    "Sleep Duration vs. Quality of Sleep across BMI Categories, colored by Stress Level",
    y=1.03,  # Adjust vertical position of the super title
    fontsize=16
)

# Set clearer axis labels for all facets
g.set_axis_labels("Sleep Duration (hours)", "Quality of Sleep (1-10)")

# Set titles for individual facets (BMI categories)
g.set_titles("BMI: {col_name}")

# Adjust the layout to prevent titles and labels from overlapping
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.98]) # Leave space for the suptitle

# Save the figure to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Do not use plt.show() as per the instructions
